title: ICE Agent Shoots Venezuelan DoorDash Driver Wilber Garces Perez in Austin, Texas
excerpt: An ICE officer shot and seriously wounded 28-year-old Venezuelan asylum seeker Wilber Rafael Garces Perez in North Austin while he was delivering food for DoorDash. His attorney said he had a valid work permit and had entered the U.S. legally; DHS disputed the account and placed him in federal custody pending removal.
content:
On September 20, 2026, a U.S. ICE officer shot Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, a Venezuelan man, once in the torso in North Austin, Texas, during what authorities described as a "small foot pursuit." He was taken to Dell Seton Medical Center in serious but stable condition.

His immigration attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, identified him as an asylum seeker with a valid work permit who had entered the United States legally. DoorDash confirmed he was in the process of making a delivery at the time of the shooting. DHS disputed his status, saying he entered illegally under the Biden administration and had a final order of removal — conflicting accounts that mirrored patterns in earlier ICE shootings.

  • The shooting was captured on video by a bystander livestreaming on Facebook, who recorded sounds of screeching tires and gunfire.
  • Garces Perez called his wife from the vehicle while "yelling in agony" immediately after being shot, according to his attorney.
  • Austin's mayor noted increased ICE operations in the city in preceding weeks; this was at least the third ICE shooting in Texas since March 2025.
  • DHS stated that Homeland Security Investigations, with FBI assistance, would lead the investigation.
  • Rep. Greg Casar warned that if ICE deported Garces Perez, "the key witness to their shooting disappears."
  • His family was reportedly denied meaningful access to information about his condition and location for hours after the shooting.

About 150 protesters gathered at the shooting scene and remained through the evening; Austin Police arrested at least one protester after dispersal orders.
source: NBC News / CNN / Texas Tribune / CBS News
